recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No further core source change is needed for FHIR-47357 unless the work group separately chooses broader editorial cleanup of neighboring subscription channel examples.
issue_request: FHIR-47357 asked whether heartbeat notifications are still required when an event notification is sent during the interval, and requested clarifying whether the heartbeat period means one heartbeat per interval or no interval should pass without a notification. The Applied/Persuasive resolution says accepted subscriptions SHOULD send a heartbeat notification when the channel has been inactive for the specified amount of time, with an example that at least one event-notification or heartbeat should occur within the interval.
initial_application: The approved source change was already present before this reconciliation. Jira comments link PR HL7/fhir#3967, and git commit 3b33a86e93c7826be974191118e4d83c2824b953 changed source/subscriptionstatus/subscriptionstatus-notes.xml from the old one-heartbeat-per-interval sentence to the current inactivity and either-notification wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists subscriptionstatus=SubscriptionStatus, confirming the checked SubscriptionStatus notes are in build scope. FHIR-I minutes for 2025-03-31 record the Subscriptions block vote including FHIR-47357 as Persuasive with a 17-0-0 motion. Zulip searches found the matching R6 Subscription Block Vote announcement and no conflicting substantive discussion.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. The current heartbeat notification section says servers SHOULD send a heartbeat notification whenever the channel has been inactive for the specified amount of time and explains that a 60-second interval means there is never a 60-second period without at least one event-notification or heartbeat.
